verdict.rationale: EFTPS publishes the main gates before you begin. Individuals can no longer enroll, so the rail is for businesses and tax professionals. Sign-in through Login.gov or ID.me is mandatory, enrollment takes up to five business days, and a PIN then arrives by U.S. Mail in five to seven business days. These facts are scattered across pages rather than set out as an exact up-front checklist, and the identity-proofing steps inside Login.gov and ID.me are not described. missing for 10: a consolidated pre-start list of prerequisites (EIN, bank details, required documents), the identity-proofing level and steps required by Login.gov/ID.me, how the PIN is used in the flow, and independent or hands-on confirmation that no steps surface mid-flow.

support.subject: As a founder, the service publishes exactly which account, credential, and identity-proofing steps stand between me and filing — stated before I start, not discovered mid-flow

citations.quote: Secure sign-in via Login.gov or ID.me is required as of October 19, 2023.
you will receive a personal identification number (PIN) via U.S. Mail in five to seven business days
New enrollments for EFTPS can take up to five business days to process.
Individual taxpayers can no longer create new EFTPS accounts.
Enroll at EFTPS or request an enrollment from EFTPS Customer Service
